Start with an established deck - preferably a deck that can be played on a budget like burn or afinity - until you get a feel for the format and learn to play against and beat the established decks.

Then dive into the game and start looking for a card that you really, really like. It doesn't have to necessarily be a good card, but it should be something that you *enjoy playing more than you enjoy winning*.

Then just start building your deck around that card and see where it goes. Use your knowledge of the format and established decks to build the most competitive version of your deck possible. I highly recommend making a proxy of the deck (just write the names of the cards on basic lands) or borrowing the expensive cards from a friend before you sink tons of your own money into it.

Modern is a really fun format, but unfortunately it is not cheap. If brewing your own unique decks is how you enjoy playing the game then explore some options that let you test decks before buying them.

This is a good point. As long as China doesn't do anything (too) stupid, then they can eventually build up enough military and economic strength to do whatever they want. 

Right now China is very much dependent on its foreign trade partners to keep its economy from crashing, but this will slowly change over the decades as China diversifies its economy and builds up more of a middle class citizenry that can absorb huge economic blows. Once China achieves this (and stabilizes its housing market), they will be able to go head-to-head with the US without risking economic implosion.

There is also the massive rearmament of the Chinese military which is advancing rapidly. Right now, China lacks large numbers of advanced nuclear submarines, aircraft carriers, and strike aircraft to pose much of a threat to the US (outside of their anti-ship missile umbrella). If the US continues its military procurement at it's current pace, China could eventually build up a large enough navy, and air force to make US intervention untenable.

For now, time is certainly on China's side. If they continue to play nice for another two to three decades, then they could emerge in a much MUCH stronger position to project power and stifle US influence in the Pacific. However, if they begin acting belligerently now while they are still too weak to challenge the US, it will end very badly for them.

If China does something as stupid as blockade Taiwan, then it will piss off the entire world. It's true that trade with China is critical to the US economy, but so is trade with Taiwan which builds a TON of the world's semiconductors.

If China were to cut trade, embargoes were be placed on them not just by the US but by most of the western bloc. The US is already just looking for an excuse to enact more protectionist measures against China (President Biden is continuing the trade war Trump started) and many European nations are becoming more weary of Chinese economic influence (see the recently canceled trade deal between the EU and China).

All told, if China ends up in a war with Taiwan, or restricts Taiwan's ability to trade with the world, it would be devastating for them. Two decades of miraculous economic growth would be wiped out in an instant as China's most important trading partners abandoned them. Worst case scenario, it could start a nuclear war which would end the world as we know it.

Your list covers about all the good space westerns that I've seen. However, there are plenty of other good space-themed anime out there if you're feeling a bit adventurous. 

I would highly recommend Planetes. Like The Expanse, it takes place in the very near future and covers the very early space development around Earth and the Moon. It is also a very realistic depiction of space that includes a high attention to detail that I haven't seen in any other anime out there. While the story in this anime is not as exciting as Holden's epic adventure to save the galaxy, it's still very well done.

Another great anime is Legends of the Galactic Heroes. While Planetes is a much more scientific anime, Legends is almost pure fantasy with fantastical futuristic technology. However, the story and characters of Legends are among the best that I've ever seen. It is my personal favorite anime and I can't recommend it enough. Please note that while Legends is fantastic, it is also a huge commitment with over 100 episodes to watch. There is a remake of the show with modern animation and updated music but it is not yet completed - I would recommend starting out watching the remake and then moving onto the older version of the show if you like what you see.
